title: TRACER: Physics-Guided Causal Evidence Construction for Zero-Shot Traffic Anomaly Diagnosis

problem.claim: Diagnosing the root causes of non-recurrent traffic congestion in large-scale networks is difficult but important for urban mobility and resilience.

gap.claim: Existing deep learning, causal discovery, and direct LLM approaches face limitations in causal identifiability, computational cost, physical guarantees, spatial hallucination, token cost, or inference latency.

contributions.claim: TRACER is a training-free agent framework for zero-shot traffic diagnosis.
Its Physics-Grounded Evidence Construction mechanism combines kinematic shockwave tracing with statistical verification to isolate causal chains.
Its Parallel Reasoning and Consensus Fusion architecture decouples complex global inferences to accelerate diagnosis and support robust localization.

author_reported_evidence.claim: On SUMO simulations and the PeMS-BAY dataset, TRACER reportedly achieves a 32.6% relative improvement in Hit@1 accuracy over state-of-the-art baselines.
The authors report an 85.7% reduction in inference time.
Closed-loop evaluations reportedly show that agent-guided interventions accelerate traffic recovery.

narrative_sequence.summary: Root-cause diagnosis of non-recurrent traffic congestion is important for urban mobility and resilience.
Large-scale traffic diagnosis is difficult, and existing learning, causal, and LLM approaches have methodological or computational limitations.
TRACER addresses these challenges with physics-grounded causal evidence construction.
Parallel reasoning and consensus fusion are used to accelerate diagnosis and improve localization robustness.
Experiments and closed-loop evaluations report improved accuracy, lower inference time, and faster traffic recovery.

source_observation.claim: The framework constructs causal evidence from physical shockwave tracing and statistical verification before model reasoning.

interpretation.claim: Constraining reasoning with domain-grounded intermediate evidence may reduce localization errors and unsupported spatial inferences.

application.claim: For zero-shot diagnosis in other physical systems, construct verified domain-specific evidence before invoking general-purpose reasoning models.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this approach transfers beyond traffic networks or under which conditions its evidence construction fails.

source_observation.claim: Complex global inferences are decoupled through parallel reasoning and consensus fusion.

interpretation.claim: Decomposing global reasoning and aggregating independent outputs may improve latency and localization robustness.

application.claim: Latency-sensitive diagnostic systems may benefit from parallel sub-inferences followed by consensus aggregation.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify the decomposition strategy, consensus mechanism, or its behavior when sub-inferences disagree.

unknowns: The abstract does not describe the training-free agent's implementation details.
The abstract does not report dataset sizes, evaluation protocols, baseline identities, or statistical uncertainty.
The abstract does not provide intervention definitions or recovery metrics.
